item.title: Clients
item.description:
Clients #

The server speaks RESP, so a Redis client works — with three adjustments: type mismatches never error, scan cursors must stay opaque, and there is no SELECT/MULTI.

redis-cli # 

redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 11001

# with TLS and auth
redis-cli --tls --cacert ./ca.crt -a "$ICEFIREDB_AUTH" -h db1.internal -p 11001

SET user:1 '{"name":"ada"}' EX 300
HGETALL user:1
SCAN 0 MATCH 'user:*' COUNT 100
XSCAN HASH "" MATCH '^user:' COUNT 100
INFO

redis-cli --scan works: it starts at 0 and loops until the cursor is 0 again.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Configuration #

The NoSQL engine has no configuration file. Every setting is a command-line flag, parsed once at startup in flags.go. (A .env file in the working directory is loaded as well — see Environment variables.)

./bin/IceFireDB -h # prints the usage block below

Basic options #

Flag Meaning Default
-a addr Bind address (host:port) 127.0.0.1:11001
-n id Node ID — also the Raft server ID and the data subdirectory name 1
-d dir Data directory data
-j addr Leader address of a cluster to join (empty — bootstrap)
-l level Log level: debug, verb, info, warn, silent info
-h Print usage and exit —

-n is an identifier, not a port. Ports come from -a. Two nodes may share -d because each one writes to <dir>/IceFireDB/<node-id>/, but two nodes must not share a node ID.

item.title: Overview
item.description:
Engine overview #

Startup sequence #

main() does a small, fixed amount of work, and the ordering matters:

  1. godotenv.Load() — pick up .env if present.
  2. confInit(&conf) — parse flags, resolve --auth from the environment, validate TLS pairing and --advertise, map --raft-backend to leveldb/bolt.
  3. conf.DataDirReady is registered as a callback: when the Raft layer has prepared the node directory it opens the storage backend (openStorage) and publishes ldb. The command handlers only work after this point, which is why /readyz exists.
  4. Backend metrics are registered with the INFO collector (hybriddb, ipfs, ipfs-synckv).
  5. --pprof and --metrics servers start, if enabled — both are plain net/http servers in goroutines.
  6. conf.Snapshot/Restore are wired to snapshot.go, connection hooks to the client counter, and rafthub.Main(conf) takes over: recover the log, join a cluster if -j was given, serve RESP.

Request path #

Writes (the 56 commands registered with AddWriteCommand):

item.title: Strings
item.description:
Strings #

26 commands: the SET family, counters, bit operations and string expiry.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
SET W SET KEY VALUE [EX seconds] [PX milliseconds] [NX] [XX] [KEEPTTL] +OK, or null when NX/XX blocks the write SET user:1 '{"n":"ada"}' EX 60 → OK
SETNX W SETNX KEY VALUE integer 1 written, 0 already exists SETNX job:42 1 → 1
SETEX W SETEX KEY seconds VALUE +OK SETEX session:9 60 tok → OK
SETEXAT W SETEXAT KEY unixTime VALUE +OK SETEXAT session:9 1767225600 tok → OK
GETSET W GETSET KEY VALUE bulk old value, null if absent GETSET counter 0 → "7"
GET R GET KEY bulk, null if absent GET user:1 → {"n":"ada"}
MGET R MGET KEY [KEY ...] array of bulk/null MGET a b → [val, null]
MSET W MSET KEY VALUE [KEY VALUE ...] +OK MSET a 1 b 2 → OK
APPEND W APPEND KEY VALUE integer new length APPEND log "x\n" → 5
STRLEN R STRLEN KEY integer length in bytes STRLEN user:1 → 13
INCR W INCR KEY integer new value INCR hits → 1
INCRBY W INCRBY KEY increment integer new value INCRBY hits 5 → 6
DECR W DECR KEY integer new value DECR hits → 5
DECRBY W DECRBY KEY decrement integer new value DECRBY hits 5 → 0
GETRANGE R GETRANGE KEY start end bulk substring (inclusive, negative offsets from the end) GETRANGE user:1 0 3 → {"n"
SETRANGE W SETRANGE KEY offset VALUE integer new length SETRANGE user:1 0 '{"m"' → 13
GETBIT R GETBIT KEY offset integer 0/1 GETBIT bitmap 7 → 0
SETBIT W SETBIT KEY offset value integer previous bit SETBIT bitmap 7 1 → 0
BITCOUNT R BITCOUNT KEY [start end [BYTE|BIT]] integer number of set bits BITCOUNT bitmap 0 0 → 1
BITOP W BITOP AND|OR|XOR|NOT destKey KEY [KEY ...] integer length of the result BITOP AND out a b → 2
BITPOS R BITPOS KEY bit [start [end [BYTE|BIT]]] integer position, -1 if not found BITPOS bitmap 1 → 7
DEL W DEL KEY [KEY ...] integer keys removed DEL a b → 2
EXISTS R EXISTS KEY [KEY ...] integer number of existing keys EXISTS a b → 1
EXPIRE W EXPIRE KEY seconds integer 1 set, 0 key absent EXPIRE session:9 60 → 1
EXPIREAT W EXPIREAT KEY unixTime integer 1 set, 0 key absent EXPIREAT session:9 1767225600 → 1
TTL R TTL KEY integer seconds left, -1 no expiration TTL session:9 → 59

Notes #

  • SET clears an existing expiration unless KEEPTTL is given. PX is rounded up to the next second because expirations are stored in whole seconds, so PX 500 keeps the key 1 s and PX 1500 keeps it 2 s — never less than asked.
  • SET ... NX/XX answers a null bulk when the condition blocks the write, not an error.
  • There is no string PERSIST: the handler exists but is commented out and not registered. To keep a value and change its lifetime, EXPIRE again or use SET … KEEPTTL.
  • EXISTS counts keys in the string keyspace only; it will not see a hash with the same name. Use HKEYEXISTS, LKEYEXISTS, SKEYEXISTS for the other types.
  • DEL deletes the string at those keys, not the same-named hash/list/set.
  • INCR/DECR on a non-numeric value answer -ERR, like Redis; a missing key is treated as 0.
  • BITCOUNT/BITPOS accept the optional BYTE/BIT unit as in Redis 7.
  • Expiry arithmetic uses the Raft clock, so a short TTL can be rejected on a node whose Raft clock lags its local clock. See Compatibility.
  • TTL is computed against the local wall clock by the storage layer, so replicas can report values that differ by their apply latency.

item.title: Building and testing
item.description:
Building and testing #

Build # 

make localbuild # bin/IceFireDB for the host platform
make run # go run . (development)
make run_dev # same, for a dev setup
make clean # remove bin/ and installed copies

Release and cross-compilation targets exist (make all, make release, make build-linux-*), but while iterating on the code use run/localbuild — the release matrix builds five GOOS/GOARCH variants per invocation.

The binary embeds its git revision and build time:

item.title: Clustering
item.description:
Clustering #

A cluster is a set of nodes that share one Raft log. Every write command is appended to that log and replayed by every node, so all nodes converge on the same state; reads are answered locally by whichever node receives them.

Bootstrapping and joining #

The first node needs no extra flag: an empty -j means “start a new cluster”. Every later node joins with -j <leader-or-any-node-address>:

item.title: Hashes
item.description:
Hashes #

19 commands. The hash keyspace is independent from the string keyspace at the same key name.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
HSET W HSET KEY FIELD VALUE [FIELD VALUE ...] integer fields added HSET user:1 name ada age 36 → 2
HSETNX W HSETNX KEY FIELD VALUE integer 1 written, 0 field exists HSETNX user:1 name ada → 0
HGET R HGET KEY FIELD bulk, null if the field is absent HGET user:1 name → ada
HMGET R HMGET KEY FIELD [FIELD ...] array of bulk/null HMGET user:1 name x → [ada, null]
HMSET W HMSET KEY FIELD VALUE [FIELD VALUE ...] +OK HMSET user:2 name bob → OK
HDEL W HDEL KEY FIELD [FIELD ...] integer fields removed HDEL user:1 age → 1
HEXISTS R HEXISTS KEY FIELD integer 0/1 HEXISTS user:1 name → 1
HGETALL R HGETALL KEY array field/value pairs HGETALL user:1 → [name, ada]
HKEYS R HKEYS KEY array of fields HKEYS user:1 → [name]
HVALS R HVALS KEY array of values HVALS user:1 → [ada]
HLEN R HLEN KEY integer field count HLEN user:1 → 1
HSTRLEN R HSTRLEN KEY FIELD integer value length, 0 if absent HSTRLEN user:1 name → 3
HINCRBY W HINCRBY KEY FIELD increment integer new value HINCRBY stats hits 1 → 1
HKEYEXISTS R HKEYEXISTS KEY integer 0/1 — does the hash exist HKEYEXISTS user:1 → 1
HCLEAR W HCLEAR KEY integer fields removed HCLEAR user:1 → 2
HMCLEAR W HMCLEAR KEY [KEY ...] integer hashes removed HMCLEAR a b → 2
HEXPIRE W HEXPIRE KEY seconds integer 1 set, 0 key absent HEXPIRE user:1 300 → 1
HEXPIREAT W HEXPIREAT KEY unixTime integer 1/0 HEXPIREAT user:1 1767225600 → 1
HTTL R HTTL KEY integer seconds left, -1 none HTTL user:1 → 299

Notes #

  • HCLEAR / HMCLEAR delete the whole hash (like DEL for this type) and take its expiration with it; HDEL removes individual fields.
  • There is no HPERSIST — the handler exists but is not registered.
  • HSET counts only newly created fields; overwriting an existing field counts 0.
  • HGETALL answers field/value pairs in the storage’s iteration order. Do not rely on it for ordering — sort client-side if it matters.
  • HGET of a field whose value is empty answers an empty bulk string on the local backends and null on the decentralized ones — the two states are not distinguishable there. See Compatibility.
  • HSTRLEN reports 0 both for a missing field and for an empty one.
  • Expiry: HEXPIRE/HEXPIREAT/HTTL act on the hash, independently of any string at the same key.

item.title: Protocol
item.description:
Protocol layer #

The engine speaks RESP — the Redis serialization protocol — so any Redis client works without a shim. This page covers what the protocol layer does beyond parsing bytes.

One socket, two protocols #

There is exactly one TCP listener (tcp4, address from -a). On it arrive:

  1. Client connections: RESP from applications.
  2. Peer connections: the Raft transport between nodes.

They are told apart by a sniffing listener: a peer opens the connection by writing a fixed magic marker followed by the cluster auth token (transportMarker in vendor/github.com/tidwall/uhaha), and anything that does not start with that marker is treated as a RESP client. This is why TLS, the port and --advertise are shared between data and replication traffic — and why --advertise must name the address peers can reach.

item.title: Benchmarking
item.description:
Benchmarking #

This page describes how to measure the engine. It deliberately contains no performance numbers: a number without the commit, hardware, backend and flags that produced it is noise.

Load generators that work #

redis-benchmark and memtier_benchmark both work, because the wire protocol is RESP.

# baseline: one connection per request, no pipeline
redis-benchmark -h 127.0.0.1 -p 11001 -t set,get -n 200000 -c 50

# pipelined
redis-benchmark -h 127.0.0.1 -p 11001 -t set,get -n 1000000 -c 50 -P 16

# mixed, with memtier
memtier_benchmark -s 127.0.0.1 -p 11001 --protocol=redis \
 --clients=50 --threads=4 --ratio=1:1 --test-time=120 --key-pattern=S:S

What they will not exercise:

item.title: Lists
item.description:
Lists #

18 commands. Lists are stored as an indexed sequence; two of these commands rebuild the whole list.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
LPUSH W LPUSH KEY VALUE [VALUE ...] integer new length LPUSH q a b → 2
RPUSH W RPUSH KEY VALUE [VALUE ...] integer new length RPUSH q c → 3
LPOP W LPOP KEY bulk head element, null if empty LPOP q → b
RPOP W RPOP KEY bulk tail element, null if empty RPOP q → c
LLEN R LLEN KEY integer element count LLEN q → 1
LINDEX R LINDEX KEY index bulk, null if out of range LINDEX q 0 → a
LRANGE R LRANGE KEY start stop array (inclusive, negative offsets from the end) LRANGE q 0 -1 → [a]
LSET W LSET KEY index VALUE +OK LSET q 0 z → OK
LTRIM W LTRIM KEY start stop +OK LTRIM q 0 0 → OK
RPOPLPUSH W RPOPLPUSH source destination bulk moved element, null if source empty RPOPLPUSH q backup → z
LINSERT W LINSERT KEY BEFORE|AFTER pivot VALUE integer new length; 0 pivot absent; -1 key absent LINSERT q BEFORE z y → 2
LREM W LREM KEY count VALUE integer elements removed LREM q 0 z → 1
LKEYEXISTS R LKEYEXISTS KEY integer 0/1 — does the list exist LKEYEXISTS q → 1
LCLEAR W LCLEAR KEY integer elements removed LCLEAR q → 1
LMCLEAR W LMCLEAR KEY [KEY ...] integer lists removed LMCLEAR a b → 2
LEXPIRE W LEXPIRE KEY seconds integer 1/0 LEXPIRE q 600 → 1
LEXPIREAT W LEXPIREAT KEY unixTime integer 1/0 LEXPIREAT q 1767225600 → 1
LTTL R LTTL KEY integer seconds left, -1 none LTTL q → 599

Notes #

  • LPUSH q a b produces [b, a] — each element is pushed to the head in turn, as in Redis.
  • LREM KEY count VALUE: count > 0 removes from the head, count < 0 from the tail, count = 0 every occurrence.
  • LINSERT and LREM are O(n) and are not transactional. The storage layer has no primitive for them, so the handler reads the list, clears it, and rewrites it (restoring the TTL). It happens inside one Raft apply, so no other client observes a partial list, but a backend failure mid-rebuild leaves the list truncated. Do not use them on long lists in a hot path — prefer LTRIM or bounded queues.
  • There is no LPERSIST: the handler is not registered. LCLEAR/LMCLEAR delete the list and its TTL.
  • No blocking commands. BLPOP/BRPOP are deliberately not registered: a blocking read inside the Raft apply loop either stalls the log or consumes the queue without a rollback path.
  • LRANGE with start > stop answers an empty array; negative indexes count from the tail.

item.title: Network
item.description:
Network layer #

Two independent networks exist, and they solve different problems. Confusing them is the most common architectural mistake when reading about IceFireDB.

Intra-site network Inter-site network
Purpose One consistent copy of the data Replicate across sites / regions
Technology Raft (hashicorp/raft) libp2p + pubsub (crdt, ipfs-log, ipfs-synckv drivers)
Topology Leader + voters, quorum required Peer-to-peer, no leader, eventual
Configured by -a, -j, --advertise, --raft-backend, --auth, TLS --servicename, --nettopic, --datatopic
Enabled by Always Only with a P2P storage backend

A common deployment runs a Raft cluster per site (strong consistency inside), with one node per site using a P2P backend to exchange data between sites (eventual consistency across). The engine does not combine the two for you — they are separate layers, and the P2P layer is a property of the driver, not of the server.

item.title: Storage backends
item.description:
Storage backends #

--storage-backend <name> selects the driver that sits under the ledis data model. The command layer is written against store.driver.IDB, so the same commands run on every backend — what changes is where the bytes live, who replicates them, and how much you can trust the driver.

type IDB interface {
 Close() error
 Get(key []byte) ([]byte, error)
 Put(key []byte, value []byte) error
 Delete(key []byte) error
 SyncPut(key []byte, value []byte) error
 SyncDelete(key []byte) error
 NewIterator() IIterator
 NewWriteBatch() IWriteBatch
 NewSnapshot() (ISnapshot, error)
 Compact() error
 GetStorageEngine() interface{}
}

What each backend is #

--storage-backend Where data lives Replication External dependency
goleveldb (default) Local LevelDB (pure Go) Raft only —
badger Local BadgerDB v4, ZSTD compression Raft only —
hybriddb Local LevelDB + Ristretto hot cache, per-driver metrics Raft only —
oss S3-compatible object store, local LevelDB index + Ristretto cache Raft only S3/MinIO endpoint
ipfs Local LevelDB whose values are fetched from IPFS by CID Raft only IPFS API (not a gateway)
ipfs-synckv IPFS as source of truth + local mirror + version metadata, optional AES-256 IPFS/ipfs-log P2P IPFS API + P2P
crdt Local Badger + icefiredb-crdt-kv over libp2p pubsub P2P CRDT libp2p peers
ipfs-log Append-only icefiredb-ipfs-log store over IPFS pubsub P2P log IPFS + P2P

leveldb (the cgo driver) and orbitdb are not compiled into the binary: the former is never imported, the latter is commented out in main.go/flags.go. Passing either name fails at startup with “unknown driver”.

item.title: Ecosystem
item.description:
Ecosystem libraries and components #

The engine is one piece. These are the libraries and services around it, all in the same GitHub organisation.

Libraries used by the storage drivers #

Project Used by What it does
icefiredb-crdt-kv driver/crdt CRDT key/value store over libp2p pubsub; merges concurrent writes without coordination
icefiredb-ipfs-log driver/ipfs-log, driver/ipfs-synckv Immutable, operation-based append-only log for distributed systems, stored in IPFS and merged through pubsub
IceFireDB/uhaha (fork) the binary Raft application framework: RESP server, log, snapshots, RAFT/CLUSTER commands
IceFireDB/ledisdb (fork) the binary The data model: per-type keyspaces, TTLs, encodings

Two of these are forked and pinned in go.mod via replace directives. Vendor updates to them are behavioural changes to the engine, so go mod vendor diffs deserve a real review.

item.title: Security
item.description:
Security #

The engine has three security-relevant surfaces: the RESP listener, the Raft transport, and the optional admin HTTP servers. They share one credential and one certificate.

Transport encryption (TLS) # 

./bin/IceFireDB --tls-cert ./server.crt --tls-key ./server.key -a 0.0.0.0:11001 -d /var/lib/icefiredb
  • Both flags are required together — providing one without the other is a startup error.
  • TLS is applied to the single listening socket. RESP clients and the Raft transport both arrive on it, and the server decides which is which by sniffing the first bytes. There is no second port.
  • The value of --advertise must therefore be the TLS address peers and clients use.
  • Clients must speak TLS too: redis-cli --tls --cacert ./ca.crt -h host -p 11001, or the equivalent client option (go-redis: TLSConfig, Python redis.Redis(ssl=True), Node tls: {}).
  • The certificate needs a DNS: SAN for the name clients use; the server copies the first DNS SAN into its tls.Config.ServerName for outbound connections.
  • No client certificates. tls.Config is built with Certificates only, so there is no mTLS and no client identity. Peers authenticate with the shared token, not a certificate.

Cluster authorization # 

export ICEFIREDB_AUTH='openssl rand -hex 32' # preferred: not visible in the process list
./bin/IceFireDB -a 0.0.0.0:11001 -d /var/lib/icefiredb
# or
./bin/IceFireDB --auth '<token>' -a 0.0.0.0:11001 -d /var/lib/icefiredb

What it does:

item.title: Sets
item.description:
Sets #

21 commands: membership, the three set-algebra families, expiry, and deterministic SPOP.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
SADD W SADD KEY MEMBER [MEMBER ...] integer members added SADD tags go db → 2
SREM W SREM KEY MEMBER [MEMBER ...] integer members removed SREM tags db → 1
SCARD R SCARD KEY integer cardinality SCARD tags → 1
SISMEMBER R SISMEMBER KEY MEMBER integer 0/1 SISMEMBER tags go → 1
SMEMBERS R SMEMBERS KEY array of members SMEMBERS tags → [go]
SDIFF R SDIFF KEY [KEY ...] array members in the first but no later set SDIFF a b → [x]
SDIFFSTORE W SDIFFSTORE dest KEY [KEY ...] integer size of the result SDIFFSTORE out a b → 1
SINTER R SINTER KEY [KEY ...] array members in every set SINTER a b → [y]
SINTERSTORE W SINTERSTORE dest KEY [KEY ...] integer size of the result SINTERSTORE out a b → 1
SUNION R SUNION KEY [KEY ...] array members in any set SUNION a b → [x,y]
SUNIONSTORE W SUNIONSTORE dest KEY [KEY ...] integer size of the result SUNIONSTORE out a b → 2
SMOVE W SMOVE source destination MEMBER integer 1 moved, 0 not a member SMOVE a b x → 1
SPOP W SPOP KEY [count] bare: bulk member; with count: array SPOP queue:ready → job:7
SRANDMEMBER R SRANDMEMBER KEY [count] bare: bulk; positive count: distinct array; negative: array with repeats SRANDMEMBER tags 1 → [go]
SKEYEXISTS R SKEYEXISTS KEY integer 0/1 — does the set exist SKEYEXISTS tags → 1
SCLEAR W SCLEAR KEY integer members removed SCLEAR tags → 1
SMCLEAR W SMCLEAR KEY [KEY ...] integer sets removed SMCLEAR a b → 2
SEXPIRE W SEXPIRE KEY seconds integer 1/0 SEXPIRE tags 60 → 1
SEXPIREAT W SEXPIREAT KEY unixTime integer 1/0 SEXPIREAT tags 1767225600 → 1
STTL R STTL KEY integer seconds left, -1 none STTL tags → 59
SPERSIST W SPERSIST KEY integer 1 removed, 0 none SPERSIST tags → 1

Notes #

  • SPOP is deterministic across replicas. Because it is a write command, its result must be identical on every node, so the picked member is derived from the Raft-seeded state rather than math/rand. With count, the count is clamped to the set size; count = 0 answers an empty array and a negative count is an error.
  • SRANDMEMBER is a read command and may use real randomness (count distinct members when positive, repeats when negative). |count| is capped at 1048576.
  • SMOVE to the same key is a no-op that returns 1 and keeps the TTL.
  • SCLEAR/SMCLEAR delete whole sets and their expiration; SREM removes members.
  • SPERSIST is the only *PERSIST command in the engine, and it is known to leave the expiration in place on the ipfs backend. Strings, hashes and lists have no PERSIST at all.
  • Set algebra commands read the sets named in the arguments; *STORE variants overwrite the destination and return the size of the result.

item.title: Storage
item.description:
Storage layer #

Under the command handlers sits ledis: a data model that turns five Redis types into key/value operations over a single driver.IDB. It is the reason the same commands work on a local LevelDB file and on IPFS.

Per-type keyspaces #

ledis does not store “a key with a type”. It stores separate physical keys per type, each prefixed with a type byte:

Type Prefix bytes Physical keys per logical key
String KVType the value
Hash HashType, HSizeType one entry per field + a size counter
List ListType, LMetaType one entry per index + a meta record (head/tail/size)
Set SetType, SSizeType one entry per member + a size counter
Sorted set ZSetType, ZSizeType, ZScoreType one entry per member + size counter + one index entry per (score, member)

Expirations are separate records too (ExpMetaType, ExpTimeType), which is why a TTL belongs to the type it was set on rather than to the key name.

item.title: Codec
item.description:
Codec layer #

The “codec” in this engine is the mapping between protocol-level structures and the KV pairs ledis writes. It is not a serialization format you can choose — it is fixed by ledis and visible only through side effects such as key limits, ordering and migration.

What gets encoded #

Logical operation Physical operations
SET k v Put(KVType + k, v)
HSET k f v Put(HashType + k + f, v), IncrBy(HSizeType + k, 1) on a new field
RPUSH k v Put(ListType + k + index, v), update LMetaType + k (head, tail, count)
SADD k m Put(SetType + k + m, nil), IncrBy(SSizeType + k, 1)
ZADD k score m Put(ZSetType + k + m, score), Put(ZScoreType + k + score + m, nil), size counter
EXPIRE k s Put(ExpTimeType + k, timestamp), Put(ExpMetaType + k, …)

Deletes are the inverse: a hash field delete removes one HashType record and decrements the size counter, while HCLEAR walks them all and removes the counters and expiry records too.

item.title: Observability
item.description:
Observability #

There are three ways to see what a node is doing: the HTTP endpoints, the INFO command, and pprof. All three are opt-in.

HTTP endpoints # 

./bin/IceFireDB --metrics --metrics-addr 127.0.0.1:11002 -d /var/lib/icefiredb
Path Response Use
/healthz 200 ok whenever the process is up Liveness probe
/readyz 200 ready once the storage backend has initialized; 503 not ready before that Readiness probe / rollout gate
/metrics Prometheus text exposition Scraping

The server is a plain http.Server with a 5-second ReadHeaderTimeout; it has no authentication, so keep it on loopback or a private interface (see Security).

item.title: Sorted sets
item.description:
Sorted sets #

15 commands. Scores are 64-bit integers, not doubles — the one difference that changes query results, not just the wire format.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
ZADD W ZADD KEY score MEMBER [score MEMBER ...] integer members added ZADD board 100 ada 90 bob → 2
ZINCRBY R ⚠ ZINCRBY KEY increment MEMBER bulk new score ZINCRBY board 5 ada → 105
ZREM W ZREM KEY MEMBER [MEMBER ...] integer members removed ZREM board bob → 1
ZCARD R ZCARD KEY integer cardinality ZCARD board → 1
ZCOUNT R ZCOUNT KEY min max integer members within the score range ZCOUNT board 0 200 → 1
ZSCORE R ZSCORE KEY MEMBER bulk score, null if absent ZSCORE board ada → 105
ZRANK R ZRANK KEY MEMBER integer rank (0-based), null if absent ZRANK board ada → 0
ZREVRANK R ZREVRANK KEY MEMBER integer reverse rank, null if absent ZREVRANK board ada → 0
ZRANGE R ZRANGE KEY start stop [WITHSCORES] array members (and scores) ZRANGE board 0 -1 WITHSCORES → [ada, 105]
ZREVRANGE R ZREVRANGE KEY start stop [WITHSCORES] array members (and scores) ZREVRANGE board 0 0 → [ada]
ZRANGEBYSCORE R ZRANGEBYSCORE KEY min max [WITHSCORES] array members (and scores) ZRANGEBYSCORE board 100 200 → [ada]
ZREVRANGEBYSCORE R ZREVRANGEBYSCORE KEY max min [WITHSCORES] array members (and scores) ZREVRANGEBYSCORE board 200 100 → [ada]
ZREMRANGEBYRANK R ⚠ ZREMRANGEBYRANK KEY start stop integer members removed ZREMRANGEBYRANK board 0 0 → 1
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE R ⚠ ZREMRANGEBYSCORE KEY min max integer members removed ZREMRANGEBYSCORE board 0 50 → 0
ZCLEAR W ZCLEAR KEY integer members removed ZCLEAR board → 1

Notes #

  • ⚠ ZINCRBY, ZREMRANGEBYRANK and ZREMRANGEBYSCORE are registered as read commands even though they mutate. Locally that is harmless; in a cluster their effect is not replicated and does not survive a leader change. Until that is fixed: compute scores client-side and write them with ZADD, and remove members with ZREM.
  • No TTL for sorted sets. There is no ZEXPIRE/ZTTL; clear and recreate the key (ZCLEAR), or keep the expiry bookkeeping in a string key.
  • Scores parse as int64. A float score such as 1.5 is rejected; WITHSCORES returns integers.
  • ZRANGEBYSCORE min max is inclusive on both ends; ZREVRANGEBYSCORE max min takes the arguments in reverse order, as in Redis.
  • ZRANK/ZREVRANK answer null for a missing member, ZSCORE likewise.
  • All range reads are ordered by score, then by member for equal scores.

item.title: Operations
item.description:
Operations #

Backup, restore, upgrade and recovery for a single node or a Raft cluster. The unit of everything is the node directory: <data-dir>/IceFireDB/<node-id>/.

What is on disk #

Path Contents Backed up by
main.db/ The ledis store in the selected driver’s format Copying the directory
store/ Raft log + stable store (leveldb or bolt) Copying the directory
snapshots/<id>/state.bin Raft state-machine snapshot: gzip header (start/ts/seed) + sds key/value stream RAFT SNAPSHOT, or copying the directory

state.bin is backend-agnostic: writeSnapshot walks the driver’s snapshot and writes key, value pairs into a gzip stream. That is why a snapshot taken on a badger node restores into a goleveldb node, while the main.db/ directory itself never does. Treat the file as opaque: copy it whole (or in RAFT SNAPSHOT READ windows) and hand it back with --restore — do not unzip or edit it.

item.title: Scan
item.description:
Scan #

8 commands in two families with two different cursor contracts. Getting them mixed up is the most common integration bug with this engine.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
SCAN R SCAN cursor [MATCH glob] [COUNT n] [TYPE type] array [cursor, keys]; cursor 0 ends the walk SCAN 0 MATCH user:* COUNT 100 → [cursor, [user:1, user:2]]
HSCAN R HSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH glob] [COUNT n] array [cursor, [field, value, ...]] HSCAN user:1 0 COUNT 10 → [0, [name, ada]]
SSCAN R SSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH glob] [COUNT n] array [cursor, [member, ...]] SSCAN tags 0 → [0, [go]]
ZSCAN R ZSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH glob] [COUNT n] array [cursor, [member, score, ...]] ZSCAN board 0 → [0, [ada, 105]]
XSCAN R XSCAN type cursor [MATCH regex] [COUNT n] [ASC|DESC] array [cursor, keys]; empty cursor ends the walk XSCAN KV "" COUNT 5 → [key:5, [...]]
XHSCAN R XHSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH regex] [COUNT n] [ASC|DESC] array [cursor, [field, value, ...]] XHSCAN user:1 "" COUNT 5 → [name, [name, ada]]
XSSCAN R XSSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH regex] [COUNT n] [ASC|DESC] array [cursor, [member, ...]] XSSCAN tags "" → [go, [go]]
XZSCAN R XZSCAN KEY cursor [MATCH regex] [COUNT n] [ASC|DESC] array [cursor, [member, score, ...]] XZSCAN board "" → [ada, [ada, 105]]

The Redis family #

SCAN / HSCAN / SSCAN / ZSCAN follow Redis’ shape but not Redis’ cursor encoding.

item.title: Server
item.description:
Server #

Three commands in the data surface. Everything else an operator needs (RAFT, CLUSTER, MACHINE, BARRIER, AUTH, SHUTDOWN, VERSION) lives in System commands.

Cmd RW Syntax Returns Example → reply
INFO R INFO bulk multi-line report INFO → # Server\r\nversion…
FLUSHALL W FLUSHALL integer keys removed FLUSHALL → (integer) 42
FLUSHDB W FLUSHDB integer keys removed — alias of FLUSHALL FLUSHDB → (integer) 42

INFO takes no arguments #

INFO memory, INFO server and INFO replication are argument errors; the command is len(args) != 1 → wrong number of arguments. Ask for INFO and read the section you need out of the single reply. The sections and their fields are documented in Observability.

item.title: System commands
item.description:
System commands #

The 110 commands in the command reference are the data surface. Under them sits a second surface, provided by the Raft/RESP layer, that operations depend on. It is not part of the Redis command set, so it is documented here.

None of these go through the Raft log unless stated, and --try-errors disables the CLUSTER family.

Connection #

Command Reply Notes
PING [message] PONG, or the message Handled before dispatch
ECHO message the message —
AUTH token OK / -unauthorized Required first when --auth is set
QUIT OK, then the connection closes —
SHUTDOWN (none — the process exits) Equivalent to SIGKILL from the client’s point of view; requires AUTH when configured

Machine #

Command Reply Meaning
VERSION bulk string Engine version, e.g. 1.0.0-rc.1
MACHINE map of now, uptime, boottime (nanoseconds) Times come from the Raft clock, so every node agrees
MACHINE HUMAN same keys as RFC3339 / duration Human-readable variant
BARRIER OK A no-op write: when it returns, every previously issued write from this client has been applied

BARRIER is how you get a read-your-writes guarantee across clients or nodes: send BARRIER on the leader, then read on a follower with --openreads.

item.title: Compatibility
item.description:
Compatibility with Redis #

IceFireDB speaks RESP and most commands behave as Redis does, but it is not Redis: the storage model underneath is ledis, which keeps one keyspace per data type and stores expirations in whole seconds. This page lists the differences a client will actually notice, and why they exist.

Behaviours marked locked by test are pinned by compat_test.go (make test-compat) so they cannot change without a deliberate update.
